title: Pak Grocery & Halal Meat Expands E-Commerce to Put Pakistani Grocery Shopping Within Reach Nationwide
text:
Wilkes-Barre, PA / Storyteller / Sep 16, 2026 /
Pak Grocery & Halal Meat expands its e-commerce presence nationwide, giving U.S. customers online access to the breadth of products typically found in a traditional Pakistani grocery store. For customers without a well-stocked South Asian market nearby, familiar staples and brands can be harder to source locally. The Wilkes-Barre-based Pakistani and South Asian grocer puts spices, desi ghee, snacks, tea, beverages, biscuits and cookies, pickles, dates, dessert mixes, and other pantry essentials into one online assortment, allowing customers to build a fuller grocery basket without depending on a specialty store nearby.
Pak Grocery & Halal Meat takes its Pakistani grocery selection beyond Wilkes-Barre and into nationwide online shopping, putting the traditional grocery trip—not just the occasional imported product—inside its e-commerce expansion. A shopping list can splinter quickly cooking ingredients come from one source, snacks and tea from another, and familiar pantry products require another search. The Pennsylvania specialty grocer pulls more of those aisles into one online destination, opening the question of how much of a traditional Pakistani grocery run can now happen without the store nearby.
A traditional grocery run only moves online when the basket can stay intact. Pak Grocery approaches Pakistani grocery shopping by connecting products that belong to the same kitchen rather than treating each specialty item as a destination of its own. A shopper preparing biryani, for example, can move from rice and boxed spices to ghee, chutney, and accompanying pantry needs without piecing the meal together product by product. The same basket can include tea, biscuits, snacks, beverages, or dessert items for later in the day.
The grocery list can stretch well beyond a single dinner. A Pakistani grocery trip can cross pantry staples, cooking essentials, breakfast foods, tea-time items, snacks, and desserts before it is complete. Beyond rice and lentils, shoppers may need flour, cooking oils, desi ghee, whole spices, pickles, chutneys, noodles, baking ingredients, dates, and other dry goods.
That broader mix is where the depth of the online assortment becomes useful.
A household can pair rice, lentils, and masalas with Pakistani snacks, tea, Pakistani biscuits & cookies, beverages, and sweets, then shop familiar names such as Shan, National, Laziza, Tapal, Rooh Afza, Peek Freans, EBM, Mehran, Falak, Qarshi, Hamdard, and Nestlé Pakistan. With more categories and familiar brands in the same place, customers can cover more of the regular grocery list in one order.
“Our goal has always been to make authentic Pakistani and South Asian grocery products more accessible to communities across the United States. We are excited to expand our e-commerce presence while continuing to serve our local customers from our Wilkes-Barre store,” said Ahsan Shoaib, Manager of Pak Grocery & Halal Meat
The Grocery List Does Not End When Dinner Does
A Pakistani grocery basket rarely belongs to one meal. Cooking ingredients may be needed for dinner, while tea, Pakistani Biscuits & Cookies, Pakistani Snacks, beverages, pickles, dates, or Pakistani dessert mixes can belong to the hours and days around it. The fewer gaps between cooking, tea time, snacking, and dessert, the less often one grocery run has to break into several.
Category depth becomes useful when those different occasions can remain connected. Pak Grocery & Halal Meat brings them into one online assortment, but the practical measure belongs to the shopper: how much of the next grocery list can stay intact from the first pantry staple to what reaches the table later?
Pak Grocery & Halal Meat Key Facts
Store and e-commerce model: Pak Grocery & Halal Meat continues serving customers from its Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, store while extending online grocery access across the United States.
Category depth: The online store organizes products across flour and atta, dals and beans, spices, beverages, biscuits and cookies, snacks, pickles, dates, dessert mixes, and other grocery categories.
Local fresh-food selection: The website also features fresh groceries and fresh halal meat, with availability and fulfillment depending on the product and location.
Frequently Asked Questions
Q: Does nationwide e-commerce replace the Wilkes-Barre store?
A: No. Pak Grocery & Halal Meat continues operating its Wilkes-Barre location while expanding online access beyond Pennsylvania.
Q: Are all products available for nationwide shipping?
A: Availability depends on the product and destination. Some fresh items are designated for local delivery, so customers should check applicable fulfillment options when ordering.
To explore Pakistani and South Asian groceries available online, visit https://pakgrocerystore.com/.
About Pak Grocery & Halal Meat
Pak Grocery & Halal Meat brings Pakistani and South Asian food shopping under one roof in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, alongside an online grocery storefront. Pantry staples, flour and atta, dals and beans, cooking ingredients, spices, snacks, beverages, desserts, pickles, dates, and familiar regional brands form the core grocery selection, while fresh groceries and halal meat add a local dimension to its Wilkes Barre operation
